title: AI Incident Reporting Under the EU AI Act — Article 62 Serious Incident Obligations
context: 2026-08-26 — Article 62 in force since 2 August 2026; providers of high-risk AI systems must report serious incidents to market surveillance authorities within 15 days
body: Under Article 62 of the EU AI Act, every provider of a high-risk AI system must report any serious incident to the market surveillance authority of the Member State where the incident occurred. A serious incident is defined as any malfunction or failure of the AI system that directly or indirectly leads to death, serious damage to health, serious and irreversible damage to property, or serious harm to the management or operation of critical infrastructure. The reporting window is tight: 15 days from the provider becoming aware of the incident. The report must include a root-cause analysis, corrective measures taken, and a timeline. This is not optional self-reporting — it is a legal obligation backed by enforcement powers under Article 71. The Council of AI's monitored containment framework provides a practical complement: continuous boundary monitoring with incident timelines that can be published as part of a verified measurement credential. When a provider publishes a signed containment-incident index alongside their Article 62 report, the market surveillance authority receives not just a narrative but a machine-readable, independently verifiable record of the incident and the provider's response.
